text: Hello everyone, welcome back to my class.We have finished reading and interaction in the last three periods.Today, we are going to learn grammar, ellipsis.By the end of this period, you are expected to increase grammatical awareness of ellipsis.Moreover, you need to distinguish the two forms of ellipsis used in the given context.And lastly, you are supposed to use ellipsis correctly in different contexts.Let's get started.Please read the two sentences below.To answer the question in another way, I would like to.What's the difference between the two answers?You can answer the question in a complete sentence or use ellipsis by omitting the part in brackets.Ellipsis is the act of leaving out some parts of a sentence.What will happen if we omit the part in brackets?The meaning doesn't change, but the answer is shorter, thus more concise.When can ellipsis be used?There are two circumstances.First, ellipsis can be used to avoid repeating information after modal verbs and other auxiliary verbs.Then, ellipsis can also be used to avoid repeating information after certain verb structures that are followed by the two infinitive.To sum up, ellipsis can be used after modal verbs, other auxiliary verbs, and the two infinitive.Now, you are going to read a transcript of a TV show on page 12.Find out what information the speakers left out in parts 1 to 6.Then, match
